chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Mu'za, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the charity (sadaqah) of property that has not yet been divided and has not yet been taken possession of, so he said: 'It is valid. The people merely intended the division (nuhlah) and thus erred.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give charity from property that has not yet been divided or possessed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of donating undivided or unpossessed property, correcting the popular juristic confusion with *al-nuhlah* (the gift of a father to a child before partition). This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in commercial and charitable transactions, emphasizing that ownership rights transfer effectively even prior to physical division or possession.
